newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Dec 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Dec 10.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- RAIL MAINTENANCE PUTS JARVIS ON RIGHT TRACK

The purchase of British Rail's Northern Infrastructure Maintenance Company for 9 million pounds stg in June is behind a huge increase in pre-tax profits for construction group Jarvis. Profits were 4.4 million pounds for the nine months to September, and takeover talk with Taylor Woodrow and Amey has resulted.
-- FLOTATIONS CAPSIZE ON ONE-DAY FALL IN SHARES

The fall in the stock market last Friday is blamed for the collapse of flotation plans for Discovery Inns, Emblem Technology and stockbroker Wise Speke. None of the cancelled flotations are expected to re-emerge for several months, and will probably be held off until after the general election.
-- RIVAL SUPPLIERS HIT BRITISH GAS

Figures have shown that British Gas is losing customers in the South West at a rate of 2,000 per week as trial competition in the supply market takes effect. The company stands to lose four million of its 20 million customers throughout the country when full competition opens.
THE TIMES
-- LANG SENDS BASS' 200 MILLION POUNDS CARLSBERG DEAL TO MMC

President of the Board of Trade, Ian Lang on Monday referred Bass' proposed 200 million pounds stg takeover of Carlsberg-Tetley to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission. The merging of the two companies would create the UK's largest brewer, controlling around 38 per cent of the market. There has already been opposition to the takeover from unions worried about further job cuts in the brewing industry.
-- INFLATION FALL EASES FEARS OF RATE RISE

A favourable set of inflation figures on Monday reduced the likelihood of a base rate rise being the outcome of Wednesday's meeting between the Chancellor and the Governor of the Bank of England. The latest figures from the Office for National Statistics showed that producer input prices fell 3.2 per cent in November, leaving input prices down 5.5 per cent from a year ago.
-- BBA PAYS 175 MILLION POUNDS FOR AMERICAN AVIATION ENGINEER

The industrial group, BBA, has bought International Airmotive, an American aerospace engineering business for 112 million pounds stg. The move is an attempt to exploit growth potential in the corporate aviation market, and will enable BBA to bridge between their existing aviation manufacturing and services activities. As part of the deal BBA will pay off 63 million pounds stg of debt.
THE GUARDIAN
-- BANK STAFF FIGHT TO HAVE CHRISTMAS EVE AFTERNOON OFF

Staff at Lloyds Bank and NatWest may strike on the afternoon of Christmas Eve, the banking union Bifu warned yesterday. The action was proposed in response to the plans by the management of both banks to scrap the traditional half-day closure on Christmas Eve.
-- ZENECA AND UNICHEM STUDY PLAN FOR 'PRIVATISED' CLINICS

Zeneca and Unichem are the likely bidders for a government pilot scheme for private health services under contract to NHS Trusts. Zeneca already runs cancer treatment centres in the U.S. and may expand the idea to Britain, while Unichem plans to experiment with 'one stop' health centres combining treatment with pharmacies. Supermarket chains are also studying expansion of their pharmacy operations.
-- BRUSSELS GETS TOUGH ON BA ALLIANCE

The European Commission anti-trust authorities have dismissed as too weak the conditions set by the British government for acceptance of the British Airways -American Airlines alliance. Britain had said that the two airlines must sell up to 168 weekly take-off and landing slots at Heathrow. The Commission is investigating whether the deal is compatible with EU competition laws.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- SHARES REBOUND AS CALM RETURNS

Shares on both sides of the Atlantic bounced back, with dealers taking the view that they had over-reacted to remarks made by Alan Greenspan the U.S. Federal Reserve chairman, on Friday. Share traders were supported by Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer, who said that financial markets had seen some over-reaction to Greenspan's comments on inflation.
-- LABOUR SET TO BRING IN CURBS ON WATER PROFITS

The Labour Party environment spokesman announced yesterday that water companies' profits could be curtailed under a Labour government. The announcement was made in Labour's second annual report on the water industry. It stated that the party is not prepared to allow soaring profits coupled with higher bills and lower investment. The report attacked price levels, claiming they have gone up by more than 40 per cent.
-- ALLIANCE POISED TO WIN FLOAT APPROVAL

The Alliance & Leicester is set to be given the go-ahead for its conversion plans at today's general meeting. Despite the threat of protests from an action group, angry at the terms of the 2.8 billion pounds stg flotation, the society expects to announce a 'yes vote' after counting the votes at the special general meeting at the London Arena. Protests from the action group will culminate in claims that the decision by the society to treat all its members equally is illegal and an abuse of members' rights.
